messages.body_plain:
Dear Altuna,

I am a Ph.D. candidate from Central South University. Nowadays I used the methylKit to perform WGBS data analysis.

I used the processBismarkAln function to read a bam file with "nolap=TRUE". I also used methRead function to read a bismarkCytosineReport file which got from the bam file. But I got different results of the total CpG. I got 11077272 rows while when read bam and got 11559081 rows when read report file.

Why did I get the different results? I performed filter using trim_galore before bismark and extracted methylation using bismark with "no-overlap". Beg for your help. Thank you.

Best,

--
--
Wang Kangli
State Key Laboratory of Medical Genetics, Changsha, Hunan, China.

messages.body_plain:
Dear Youngjune,

If I understood correct you want to filter an methylBaseDB object based on an methylDiff object. The following snippet could achieve this:

```
data("methylKit")

## get the DMRs
hyper.dmr <- getMethylDiff(.Object = methylDiff.obj,type = "hyper")
hyper.dmr

## filter methylBaseDB based on DMRs
hyper.mbase <- selectByOverlap(methylBaseDB.obj,ranges = as(hyper.dmr,"GRanges"))
hyper.mbase

## cluster
PCASamples(hyper.mbase)

```

Please note:
"hyper.mbase" will be an in-memory methylBase object and to save as DB again use makeMethylDB().
Besides, this will work independently of using methylDB or normal methylKit objects.

Best,
Alex

Hello,

The earlier problem you found actually related to the reading of initial data (methylRawDB), not intermediate, like methylBaseDB.
But, we are currently working on new features, which are not yet available, to make reading and writing of the tabix objects easier.

So if you have the latest version of methylKit from GitHub (v1.3.3), then you could use this code to load for example the data inside a tabix file:

methylKit:::readMethylBaseDB(dbpath = methylBaseDB.obj@dbpath,
                             dbtype = "tabix", sample.ids = met...@sample.ids,
                             assembly = met...@sample.ids, context = methylBaseDB.obj@context,
                             resolution = methylBaseDB.obj@resolution, treatment = c(1,1,1,1),
                             destranded = methylBaseDB.obj@destranded)

If you have any questions related to the function call please ask.

Please note:
This function is not exported and probably will never be, this is why you have to call it like this 'methylKit:::readMethylBaseDB'.

Best,
Alex
